data.name: Zedekia
data.gender_notes: Zedekia is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew root 'zedek', meaning 'just, righteous, or righteousness'. In the Bible, Zedekia was a king of Judah who reigned during the Babylonian captivity. He is known for his loyalty to God and his eventual repentance. The name Zedekia carries the meaning “Just, righteous, or righteousness” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zedekia usually hope their child will grow to embody just, righteous, or righteousness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes loyalty and devotion to God
data.etymology: Zedekia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Just, righteous, or righteousness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Zedekia total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: צדקיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: צדקיה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'האל יקים צדק' או 'צדק אלוהים'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'צדק' שפירושו צדק או צדיק, ו'יה' שפירושו אלוהים. השם צדקיה מופיע בתנ'ך כמלך יהודה האחרון לפני גלות בבל.

in_greek.name: Ζεδεκίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ζεδεκίας είναι το ελληνικό ισοδύναμο του εβραϊκού ονόματος צדקיה, που σημαίνει 'Δικαιοσύνη Θεοῦ' ή 'Θεός δικαίος'. Το όνομα προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή γλώσσα και χρησιμοποιήθηκε στην αρχαία Ελλάδα για να αναφερθεί στο βασιλιά της Ιουδαίας.

in_latin.name: Zedekia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Zedekia significat 'Deus iustitiam statuit' vel 'Iustitia Dei'. Nomen hebraicum צדקיה transliteratum est in linguam latinam. In traditione christiana, nomen Zedekia refertur ad regem Iudaeae ultimum ante exilium Babylonis.

in_english.name: Zedekia
in_english.long_meaning: Zedekia is a Christian name derived from the Hebrew name צדקיה, meaning 'God establishes righteousness' or 'righteousness of God'. The name is composed of two elements: 'tsedek' meaning righteousness, and 'Yah' referring to God. In the Bible, Zedekia was the last king of Judah before the Babylonian exile. The name holds significant spiritual meaning, symbolizing God's justice and righteousness.

data.cultural_impact: Zedekia reflects the cultural and spiritual values of the Biblical tradition and is used in Christian communities.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Zedekia stands as a reminder of the importance of living a just and righteous life, following God's teachings and striving for holiness. It encourages us to repent and turn back to God when we stray from His path, as King Zedekia did during the Babylonian captivity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zedekia: Righteousness of the Lord. A name given to kings who sought God's justice and rule, symbolizing God's faithfulness and the ideal monarch's commitment to uphold divine law.

biblical_reference.note: Zedekia was the last king of Judah, reigning from 597 to 586 BCE.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Zedekia was the last king of Judah, ruling from 597 to 586 BCE during the Babylonian Captivity. The name Zedekia carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Babylonians, under King Nebuchadnezzar, had conquered Judah and taken the Jewish king, Jeconiah, into exile. Zedekia was a vassal king placed on the throne by Nebuchadnezzar.

historical_references.reference: Zedekia rebellion against Babylon (589-582 BCE) resulted in the final destruction of the Temple and the exile of the Jews to Babylon.
historical_references.context: Zedekia, despite being a vassal king, attempted to rebel against Babylonian rule. This led to a series of battles and ultimately the final conquest of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar. The Second Temple was destroyed and thousands of Jews were taken into exile in Babylon.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Zedekia is of biblical origin, derived from the Hebrew language meaning 'righteous or just'. It gained modern relevance in various contexts, including literature and media, academic research, and archaeology. In literature and media, Zedekia is a character from the Old Testament, who served as the last king of Judah before the Babylonian conquest. His story has been adapted in numerous works, such as the 1958 novel 'The King's Two Bodies' by Thomas Starkey, and the 1980s anime 'Mazinger Z' which features a character named Zedekiya. In academic research, scholars continue to study Zedekia's reign and its historical significance, with a focus on his political and religious context. In archaeology, excavations at sites such as Jerusalem and Babylon have unearthed artifacts related to the time of Zedekia, providing valuable insights into the ancient world. Overall, the name Zedekia remains an important and relevant figure in the study of biblical history and ancient civilization.
